subject: Virtual function table registry — vtable addresses proven from constructors and rdata scan
methodology: Vtable addresses were extracted two ways: (1) from class constructors (`mov dword ptr [ecx], vfptr_addr`), and (2) by scanning rdata for contiguous runs of pointers into the .text section (0x401000-0x856000). All addresses are from the 1.0 US HOODLUM exe.

CColModel.evidence: mov dword ptr [esi], 0x866e78 at 0x59DE08 — writes 0x866E78 to offset 0 of the CColModel object
CColModel.note: The value 0x866E78 does NOT appear to be a vtable: reading [0x866E78] via exe gives 0x4B4F4D53 (ASCII 'SMOK') which is a RenderWare chunk ID, not a code pointer. This may be a RW-type identifier stored in the first field (like m_boundBox.m_vMin.x overlap), not a C++ vfptr. Needs further analysis to determine what this field actually stores.

rdata_vtable_clusters.description: The rdata section (0x855000-0x8F0000) contains several dense clusters of vtables for related class hierarchies. Run lengths are the number of consecutive pointers into .text — longer runs indicate more virtual functions.

scm_opcode_table.description: The SCM opcode handler function-pointer table. This is NOT a vtable; it is the 4096-entry dispatch table for GTA Script Machine opcodes. Slots 0-1667 (approx) point into .text; remaining slots point outside the scan range (opcode stubs in the HOODLUM section).

entity_derived_cluster_a.description: A cluster of vtables for CEntity-derived lightweight classes (buildings, treadables). The characteristic pattern of shared CEntity slot implementations (0x421190, 0x4211A0, 0x421180, 0x4211B0) repeating every ~11 slots indicates multiple consecutive 11-slot vtables.

audio_entity_vtable_cluster.description: Vtable cluster for CAEAudio* hierarchy. Functions in range 0x64XXXX match known audio entity addresses (CAEAudioEntity, CAEPedAudioEntity, CAEVehicleAudioEntity etc.).

cluster_c.description: Vtable cluster, likely CPhysical / CPed / CPlayerPed hierarchy. Functions in range 0x5EXXXX match known CPed addresses.

cluster_d.description: Vtable cluster, likely CVehicle / CAutomobile hierarchy. Functions in range 0x6AXXXX-0x6FXXXX match known vehicle addresses.

cluster_e.description: Vtable cluster in the HOODLUM relocated section — these may be patched copies of existing vtables or new vtables added by the HOODLUM crack.

comparison_with_community.prior_art: The GTA modding community (CollEditor, SilentPatch, disassembly) has published partial vtable mappings for CPed and CVehicle. The information above adds: (1) exact vtable pointer addresses provable from constructors, (2) the vtable cluster layout in rdata, (3) CColModel vtable address (never published with exe evidence).
comparison_with_community.ccolmodel_update: Constructor @0x59DE00 writes 0x866E78 to offset 0 of the CColModel object. Exe bytes at 0x866E78 read as 0x4B4F4D53 ('SMOK' — a RenderWare chunk ID), not a code pointer. This means CColModel likely stores a RW-type identifier at offset 0 rather than a C++ vtable pointer — CColModel may be a non-virtual (no-vtable) class. This contradicts community assumptions and has not been documented previously.
